topic: Why can more choices make decisions worse?
centralQuestion: Why can an added option make choosing harder?
commonIntuition: More options should make it easier to find a good fit.
counterintuitiveResult: A larger choice set can add comparison work and delay a decision.
mechanism: Each new option adds another comparison.
The decision can feel harder even when every option is acceptable.
visualMetaphor: A small group of paths gradually branches into a dense field of routes.
endingInsight: An option has value only when it helps someone choose.

suggestedSceneFlow.purpose: Contrast more options with harder choosing.
Show a person and a small set of choices.
Add options and show comparison effort rise.
Compare a smaller and a larger choice set.
Show how more options can delay choosing.
Connect comparison work to decision friction.
Close with a quiet insight about useful choice.

riskFlags.claim: A named psychology study established a precise ideal number of choices.
riskFlags.reason: A study and numerical claim require independent source verification.
